title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
abstract: arXiv:2608.11408v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prior white-box studies show that large language models can retain latent traces of target knowledge after unlearning, even when the knowledge is no longer expressed in their outputs. However, existing audits remain limited to one-off diagnostics: it is unclear whether these residual signals can predict future recovery under continued training or serve as reliable optimization targets. Resolving this gap is essential to determine whether internal auditing can move beyond post-hoc evaluation toward proactive risk monitoring and safer unlearning. We propose J-Access, an inference-time audit that uses the Jacobian lens to map intermediate representations into vocabulary space and measures how often target concepts remain accessible along the model's output pathway. translated_title: 衡量而非优化：预测大语言模型遗忘中的恢复
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11408v1 公告类型：新论文。摘要：先前的白盒研究表明，大语言模型在遗忘后，即使目标知识不再在其输出中表达，仍能在潜在痕迹中保留这些知识。然而，现有的审计仍局限于一次性诊断：尚不清楚这些残余信号能否预测在持续训练下的未来恢复，或作为可靠的优化目标。解决这一差距对于确定内部审计是否能超越事后评估，迈向主动风险监控和更安全的遗忘至关重要。我们提出J-Access，一种推理时审计方法，利用雅可比透镜将中间表示映射到词汇空间，并衡量目标概念在模型输出路径上的可访问频率。我们假设残余可访问性反映了恢复敏感性：离输出路径更近的知识需要更少的微调来恢复，从而可能导致更快的恢复。
tldr: 本文提出J-Access，一种利用雅可比透镜的推理时审计方法，通过衡量目标知识在模型输出路径上的可访问性来预测遗忘后的恢复敏感性，从而将内部审计从事后评估转向主动风险监控。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes J-Access, an inference-time audit using the Jacobian lens to measure the accessibility of target knowledge along the output pathway, predicting recovery susceptibility after unlearning and shifting internal auditing from post-hoc evaluation to proactive risk monitoring.
